common_name: Archiduchesse Elisabeth d'Autriche Rose (Pink Hybrid Perpetual)

planting.note: Set out bare-root or container-grown, own-root plants in spring or fall in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; this nearly thornless Hybrid Perpetual needs little support but benefits from generous feeding to sustain repeat bloom.

directions: Bred by Moreau-Robert in France and introduced in 1881, this Hybrid Perpetual produces large, very full, flat-globular blooms of medium pink washed with mauve on an upright, nearly thornless shrub. Rather than flowering only once, it repeats in successive flushes from late spring into fall, each bloom carrying a moderate, classic old-rose scent. Grow it in fertile, well-drained soil with routine deadheading between flushes, and prune lightly in late winter to remove old or crossing wood. It is historically notable as the parent rose from which the striped sport Vick's Caprice later arose.
